title: First newborn checkup
what: A pediatrician and nurse examine your baby in the first days after you leave the maternity hospital. They often come to your home.
why: For all newborns after discharge from the maternity hospital.
tell_doctor: How the birth went and what you were told at the hospital
How your baby feeds and how many wet diapers a day
If the skin is turning yellow
How the umbilical cord stump is healing

prepare.title: Documents
prepare.text: Keep the hospital discharge papers and your baby's documents at hand.

prepare.title: Questions
prepare.text: Write down questions about feeding, sleep, and bathing so you do not forget.

prepare.title: Space
prepare.text: Prepare a changing table or a clean surface where your baby can be examined.

steps: The doctor asks about the birth and how you both are
The skin, head, eyes, and cord stump are checked
The doctor listens to the heart and lungs and checks reflexes
Feeding is observed, and the doctor helps if needed
Care and warning signs are explained
feel: Your baby may cry when undressed. That is normal
after: The next checkup is usually at 1 month
Care for the cord stump as the doctor showed you
Call the clinic whenever you are unsure
red_flags: Your baby is floppy, feeds poorly, or does not wake for feeds: call emergency services
A temperature over 38°C (100.4°F), or cold, pale skin: call emergency services
Jaundice gets worse, or the skin is yellow down to the legs
The cord stump is red, oozing, or smells bad

faq.q: Is it normal for my baby to look a little yellow?
faq.a: Mild yellowing in the first days is common. Show it to the doctor, who will say if it needs checking.
Usually on demand, often 8 to 12 times a day. The doctor will check that your baby is getting enough.

reminders.text: Your baby's first checkup is tomorrow. Have the hospital discharge papers and your questions ready.
